title: Defenders of the Realm - detailed game discussion / customizing play for two heroes
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VvVtNiE0bjA

Daniel (@dungeondive) follows up his casual *Defenders of the Realm* chat with the gameplay detail it skipped, played live from a game in progress. The premise is that four heroes is the balanced party, and that by the endgame four hands of cards and twelve abilities leave him overwhelmed — so this is an experiment in playing two, the cleric and the monk, each granted one extra action token to compensate.

The walkthrough is a good tour of the machinery: action tokens double as hit points, so wounds directly cost you turns; movement by foot, horse, eagle or magic gate is paid for in colour-matched hero cards; generals must be killed outright or they regenerate. His modular stack is Legends (an extra legendary power per hero), the expanded quest deck, Companions with its events resolved before recruits, the Tainted Rose ship touring four port cities, eighteen special cards, and Winds of War as the counterweight — every special ability played feeds a deck that periodically fires something brutal back.

The best passage is accidental. A failed quest about black barges dumps minions across every port on the first turn; the replacement quest drawn is about recruiting pirates in the same waters. This is what he loves in the game — a story you generate rather than read, an epic conflict emerging without a line of narrative text.

----

Do you scale co-op games down to fewer heroes for manageability, or does that break the balance the designer built around a full party?
